title: Compatible system of semisimple characters: hypothesis (T1)–(T5)
body_html:
Compatible system of semisimple characters $\Phi$

Setting: $\BSigma$ is a generalized building (see Generalized building B(Σ) = G ×^K A) satisfying (K1)–(K3), (F1)–(F2), (F3)–(F5).

A compatible system of semisimple characters is a pair $\Phi = (\mathscr{K}_+, \phi)$ where, for each $x \in \BSigma$, $\mathscr{K}_{+, x} = K_{x,+}$ is an open subgroup of $\hat K_x = \Fix_G(x)$ and $\phi_x : K_{x,+} \to R^\times$ is a character. We write $\phi_\mathcal{F} := \phi_x$ for any $x \in \mathcal{F}$ (by axiom (T1)).

Hypothesis (Type)

(T1) $\mathscr{K}_+$ and $\phi$ are constant on each facet of $\BSigma$.

(T2) $K_{\mathcal{E},+} \subseteq K_{\mathcal{F},+}$ and $\phi_\mathcal{E} = \phi_\mathcal{F}|_{K_{\mathcal{E},+}}$ for $\mathcal{E} \subseteq \overline{\mathcal{F}}$ — i.e. $\mathscr{K}_+$ is a sheaf of subgroups and $\phi$ is a sheaf of characters.

(T3) $G$-equivariance: $K_{gx,+} = {}^g K_{x,+}$ and $\phi_{gx} = {}^g \phi_x$.

(T4) Intertwining: for $x, y \in A$ and $g \in G$, $$\Hom_{{}^g K_{y,+} \cap K_{x,+}}({}^g \phi_y, \phi_x) \ne 0 \;\Longleftrightarrow\; g \in K_x M K_y \;\Longrightarrow\; gy \in K_x \mathcal{B}(M).$$

(T5) Geodesic factorization: for $z \in [x, y]$, $$K_{z,+} = (K_{x,+} \cap K_{z,+})(K_{y,+} \cap K_{z,+}).$$

(T4) and (T5) are the deep input axioms. They are verified for classical groups (see [[node:applications.classical_T_axioms]]) and for tame types (see [[node:applications.tame_T_axioms]]).

Consequence of (T4) used in §7.2: the character-agreement statement

(T4b) — character agreement. For any $x, y \in A$, the characters $\phi_x$ and $\phi_y$ agree on $K_{x,+} \cap K_{y,+}$.
proof_html:
Apply (T4) with $g = e$. The right-hand side becomes $e \in K_x M K_y$, which is true (always). Hence the left-hand side forces $\Hom_{K_{x,+} \cap K_{y,+}}(\phi_y, \phi_x) \neq 0$. Both sides of the Hom are 1-dimensional characters of $K_{x,+} \cap K_{y,+}$; non-orthogonality of two characters is equivalent to equality (a character of $H$ either equals another character of $H$ or is orthogonal to it in $\Hom_H$, the latter by Schur). So $\phi_x|_{K_{x,+} \cap K_{y,+}} = \phi_y|_{K_{x,+} \cap K_{y,+}}$. $\square$

This is the form of (T4) actually consumed by the unconditional geodesic-telescoping identity (iii) of [[node:coefficient_systems.idempotent_system_from_T_axioms]].
